label: 4th original token after an f/n/0 ... o/3 prefix (e.g. "f r o _", "f o o _")
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t == 3) & isin(first_tok, [tok("f"), tok("n"), tok("0")]) & isin(prev_tok, [tok("o"), tok("3")]) & isin(prev2_tok, [tok("o"), tok("r"), tok("l"), tok("3"), tok("h"), tok("0")]) & isin(in_tok, [tok("n"), tok("g"), tok("v"), tok("a"), tok("z"), tok("q")])
explanation: Very sparse feature (about 0.003% of steps). It fires almost only in the original phase (88% of mass), mostly at step 3 (68% of mass) with some at step 4. The 4-token prefix it needs is narrow: first token f, n or 0; previous token o (lift 25x) or 3; the token two back usually o, r, l, h or 3; and the current input usually n, g, v, a, z or q. Typical strongest examples are "f r o [v]", "f o o [v]", "0 r o [g]" and "n h 3 o [g]". Magnitude is fairly flat (median 0.12, max 0.16); the top examples are full f-r-o / f-o-o / n-h-3-o prefixes. It never fires at steps 0-2 or on the delimiter, and rarely in the copy phase. The rule is a conjunction of token identities with no clear shared meaning, and many combinations that match the token sets stay silent (e.g. "n 0 o v", "n r 3 a"). It reads more like one region of the hidden state that some specific prefixes reach than a clean concept. Dev F1 is about 0.51.
